Developed by Infinite Interactive and published by D3Publisher Of America Inc., Puzzle Quest: Galactrix is yet another puzzle roleplaying game in Infinites steadily growing stable of quality match 3 titles. The wonderful thing about this game, however, that sets it apart from the other Puzzle Quest titles is that this one does not take place in a fantasy setting. No dragons, no swords and no magic. Galactrix instead is set far into the future and deals with aliens, lasers and technology. You take on the role of a rogue M.R.I. pilot scouring the galaxy in your spaceship trying to uncover clues in an intergalactic mystery that will affect the fate of the entire universe.
I'm happy to report that the addictive match 3 gameplay is back but with an all new redesigned puzzle battlefield as well. Gone are the circular gems of the fantasy based Puzzle Quest titles. They have been replaced by the more futuristic looking hexagonally shaped tiles and since this game takes place in space gravity will be a factor in how the tiles fall. If the match takes place in orbit around a planet, the tiles will always fall downward but if you are fighting in open space the tiles will come from whatever direction you made your previous move so strategy will also be a factor in how you battle. The puzzle play is the same as always, you try to match 3 or more colored tiles with each color representing a different aspect of your spacecraft such as weapons, shields, engineering, computer, psi and intel.
Combat in this game takes place between spaceships. Your chosen vessel can be outfitted with a plethora of different equipment and armaments which are the equivalent of spells and bladed weapons in the fantasy based Puzzle Quest games. These items use gunnery, engineering, science and shield energy corresponding with the different colored tiles respectively. Make enough matches and build up the appropriate amounts of energy and you will be able to use that piece of equipment or weapon on your opponents ship. Take down your enemies shields and do enough damage to the hull and you will be victorious. Victories will earn you intel, which is the equivalent of experience points, which you can then use to upgrade the level of your character giving the player bonuses to different abilites. Another method of damaging your opponents vessel besides using your weapons is by matching the numbered tiles. These mine-like tiles have a different number 1-10 indicating the power of the damage output so matching higher numbers will be devastating to either you or your enemy. Throughout the course of the game, you will be able to salvage or buy a number of different ships each with it's own unique options and upgrade potentials. Some of the ships will blow your mind in both their design and specifications but they will not be easy to accquire. If you want a top of the line ship you'll have to save your credits, do a little haggling or get your hands on some unique schematics and just build your own. As I mentioned earlier, there is also a large abundance of equipment and weapons that you can accquire to further augment your warship such as laser turrets, shield generators, repair drones, etc.. For example shield inhibitors, which are my personal favorite, cause your opponents shields to stall out and not regenerate which leaves their hull completely open to attack. WWCPD...What Would Captian Picard Do? Depending on your playstyle you'll definitely find the right combination of technology to suit you if you buy it, loot it or craft it.
The story is quite compelling as it involves you solving a big mystery so you want to keep playing in order to see what pieces of the puzzle, no pun intended, you can put together and what questions you can answer. The graphics are top notch and this is definitely one of the more amazing looking match 3 games. Anyone who is a fan of science fiction will appreciate the beautiful handrawn art of the various alien species, unique worlds and especially the different makes and models of spaceships, weapon arrays and equipment showcased in this gorgeous game. The musical score is excellent filled with an abundance of surreal, jolly and haunting tracks which fit the titles futuristic theme perfectly. Sound effects are also quite superb. You'll love the combat sounds of the various weapons systems, the impact of the explosions and the sound of your system crashing when your opponent uses some kind of sabotage tech on your computer as well as a number of other terrific effects. Besides the combat puzzles there are also a variety of different puzzle types which involve hacking, mining, crafting, haggling and gathering rumors.
Puzzle Quest: Galactrix is just so much fun and highly addictive. One gripe I do have about this title concerns gameplay. The game is completely random yet sometimes it seems as though your A.I. opponent receives and matches multiple damage tiles so many more times than you do to the point of sheer ridiculousness. I can't tell you how many times I've lost a battle because so many moves that I would make would yield nothing for me yet set the A.I. up for devastating damage against me time after time to the point of me rage quitting....oh it's so frustrating! With that said, this is still one of the best match 3 games I've had the pleasure of playing and I will continue to enjoy this title for years to come. If you've ever found yourself watching an episode of Star Trek or a similiar science fiction show and dreaming of commanding a spaceship in an epic battle then this game does a great job of delivering that experience to you. Puzzle Quest: Galactrix is highly recommended for any match 3, sci-fi or strategy gamer.

This is one of the most well made games I have ever played. I loved Bladestorm on Playstation 3, I wanted to love it on PC too, but there are just so many problems with the engine that Koei has used that it is barely playable for anyone who uses a decent nVidia GPU, so unplayable that you'll be spending a lot of your playtime trying to figure out how to fix the issue or booting the game back up when it's decided to randomly crash either before battle, mid battle, after battle or when you get to tavern.
I personally, do not care about the graphics, I don't care that they don't look as good as current generation games, I could accept the frame drops in battles, hell, I'd even accept the odd crash here and there; but not every battle, or every other battle, or every 20 - 30 minutes I get to play. Steam's refund policy came after this was released, so a lot of us got stung by that, because we spend more then '2 hours' trying to find a way to play the game, or we waited desperately for Koei to say something, but they didn't.
Instead, they moved on to Toukiden: Kiwami, another Playstation 4 Port, where they then said they found an issue with certain nVidia cards. Then, the reports came in again, from nVidia users, that they have constant crashing issues, including owners that are not on the list of the cards listed to have a problem. Like Bladestorm, the issues where with 'Windows 8.1' and yet the game is listed to be compatable with 'Windows 8.1' but if you own certain cards, by nVidia, you have to run it in Windows 7 to get it to work... if you're so lucky.
Then you had the fixes, rolling back drivers to older ones, Windows 7 Compatability, turning everything down to low, turning things off. It's not acceptable and as someone who has followed Koei's releases on Consoles way back from Dynasty Warriors 2, I find it extremely saddening that Koei are giving us PC Gamers, games that are unstable, broken or extremely restricted to certain hardware. It isn't fair, especially with the price they're asking and it isn't right; and despite being a fan of Koei's games, I'd honestly say that if Bladestorm and Kiwami are what we can expect to get from them, then avoid unless you have an AMD Card, or one of the few nVidia GPU's that seem to be working without issue.
Or, you have Windows 7. God help us when Windows 10 comes out.

After waiting for the final DLC I finally got around to finishing the game (Ironman Commander for those interested) and I can say with certainty that I absolutely adore this game. I was originally introduced to the previous game last year by a friend, and I found it to be a refreshing experience after so long playing MOBAs among other things. So, after getting addicted to that one it was only natural to assume the same result would occur for XCOM 2. It did. A lot of the free time I had the past week was dedicated to XCOM 2 where I ended up running an Ironman Legendary + Ironman Commander campaign simultaneously. I am still yet to finish the legendary run but that will hopefully not be too far off! Anyway, enough waffling as there is just so much about XCOM 2 that needs to be tackled.
I, like most others, purchased XCOM 2 prior to release as I was very excited for the game. There are other strategy games of this type out there but I feel that XCOM executes everything very nicely, and despite a few glitches here and there (along with apparent optimisation issues!) it was a very fluid experience. I believe, however, that most optimisation issues have been resolved for most people since release. Of course, consulting the specifications the game requires would also go some way to avoiding any problems. It is my understanding that you are no doubt excited by your brand new integrated graphics processor but I should warn you now to expect issues. As far as glitches go I've only encountered these particular issues:
There are probably more that other people have encountered but these were the ones I came across. This does not mean the game is a broken mess, but it is definitely far from perfect! Despite these issues I would wholeheartedly recommend this game.
On the topic of graphical glitches let's talk about the graphics themselves. I have to say that the art direction for the game is absolutely beautiful. The Aliens look amazing, the environments look amazing, the full moon the cinematic camera gives me whenever a Sectoid appears looks amazing... the game just looks amazing. Compared to the previous game the graphics are years apart. Four years, to be specific. It might not be the most 'realistic' looking game but it definitely looks great. I was particularly happy with the fact that pretty much all of the environment is destructable, and impressed with how good it looked getting destroyed.
The art direction for the Aliens this time around seemed to be hitting the 'very creepy' and 'very aesthetic' notes. From the highly defined curves of the Sectoid derrière to the chiseled chest of the Archon the aliens truly are a fearsome sight to behold! It's no wonder with Aliens that look this good that the world stood little chance before being overwhelmed. I certainly didn't. The Advent forces followed a much more geometrical design, and it was a nice contrast to the curves flaunted by the Aliens but it's definitely clear that Aliens themselves were the main focus of the artists.
As far as the gameplay goes it's more of the same if you've played the previous XCOM. If you haven't then it can be easily described as 'addicting'. Long gone is the concept of "just... one... more... turn" as it is essentially replaced by the more apt "just... one... more... day". Hold on, day??? I am of course referring to the Geoscape. Once you've finished the initial introductory mission you're cast into the world of XCOM. The Resistance is ready to kick the resistance into full-throttle and you'll be doing that one scan at a time. Most actions taken on the Geoscape will require several days to complete and in that time you'll be involved in guerilla operations, council requests and mostly twiddling your thumbs while waiting for either of the above to occur. By no means is this boring, though! The excitement when Tygan finally perfects duct-taping a scope to your rifles, before passing it to Shen to perform said duct-taping, is gripping.
When you're not staring at the Geoscape you'll be managing the Avenger's facilities, constructing facilities, powering facilities and facilitating facilities. The base-management aspect of the game is pretty straight-forward but it is definitely important to pay attention to the adjacency bonuses! There isn't a huge selection of facilities to choose from but there aren't that many places to put them either. It balances out in a weird sorta way.
Finally, the Battlescape is where you'll spend the majority of your time. If you're familiar with the previous XCOM then this will mostly feel the same... except it's not. Part of the Resistance experience is that you now begin most missions concealed, and with a number of turns in which you must complete your objective. Nobody said this was going to be easy. The concealment mechanic is something of an odd feature as many people have fallen victim to the idea that this means you can take the stealthy approach to missions. While it is possible the AI tends to make a bee-line for you once you get close enough to the objective. In most cases this will result in your squad getting surrounded, passed around, and killed in a most gruesome way. Therefore, it is best to instead treat the concealment as a chance to get into a good position to do the above to your enemy instead.
Another gripe most people have is with the turn timers. I will admit that, at first, they can seem overwhelming to the point that you feel the need to dash in order to keep up. I assure you that if you keep your cool and have a plan that you will find the timers mean very little. If this is still an issue then the workshop should have a mod to disable the turn timers so you can play at your own pace! It truly is a game for everyone.
I will just briefly also give my opinion on the DLCs:
I LOVED Shen's Last Gift and the Alien Hunters. The Spark is such an adorable robot, and there's something satisfying about wearing your enemies as protection. I'm not really a big fan of the Anarchy's Children cosmestics, though. If you're into making your squad look like clowns or whatever then you might enjoy it.
Um, so, overall there's so much to talk about with XCOM 2 but I feel that it's an experience best experienced! I give it two paws up.

I'd say that a large amount of the reviews are simply unfair hate with possible neglected attention when it comes to settings.
To get it out the way, you can change the language to English via the Configuration Launcher, Its in a dropdown menu in the 2nd Tab I think. As for Frames it should be fixed by turning off the VSYNC, if you still have issues turn of some of the extra options like Anti Alias AO Shading etc ie things with an OFF option. Adding "Run in compatablility mode" is supposed to also help with issues, I did this to all 4 .exe's just to be sure. Also bear in mind that while Frames may be low in the Tavern, they are usually good in the actual game (or at least they were for me).
In terms of crashes, I have only experienced them during the Nightmare storyline. I did not have any while doing The Hundred Years War Storyline which is the bulk of this game. I would also like to add that these crashes have occured after running the game (as in No lifeing it) for pretty much 4 days straight if a bit less, so maybe some fatigues on the system as its quite hot where I am at the moment.
As for the game itself, I thinks its a wonderful remake and improvement of the original BLADESTORM: The Hundred Years War, with its extra features making the game a bit more dynamic if a bit easier at times (I'm specifically refering to having access to up to 3 extra mercenaries, combined with the fact you can now decide what your default unit is, so feel free to spam horses all day).
All in all I really enjoyed replaying this remake and have not regretted my time invested in the game. The changes to the system while simple have made it different enough to enjoy replaying and my only really gripe would be the fact that they didn't think to make life easier for players buying bulk items, as you have to buy and equip each item indvidually on each character you are using, which is fairly annoying when managing more than 4 characters, and even then it can get tedious. At the same time it would also have been nice to compare stats in the menu's to characters other than my main character, as I have to go through menu's to check it in comparison to my other characters gear, which is again another minor gripe.
On the plus side however, it is worth noting that SP is now shared accross all books so if you have a certain type of book you need to level but hate using, (I'm looking at you Chariot and Engineer) you can feel free to farm the SP via another book on another character and simply use the Unit type once for a specific mission in game. A boon of which I have really appreciated, alongside being able to play as Units other than just custom Mercenaries.
Moving on to the Nightmare storyline, I have really enjoyed the freshness it has bought to the series, though I do feel its a bit short while extremely challenging at times. I say this as a player who has entered Nightmare mode with a complete character who's very high level in most the Units I prefer (Yes Level 99 Lancers FTW).
So while I look forward to going back through it again to pick back up all the special new versions of existing Units and actual Units (Like Dragon) I am not exactly sure as to whether I can warrent the £50 I have paid for the game. I cannot pretend I have not had a very good time out of the storyline, the replay value thats been added or the prospect of replaying the "The Hundred Years War" Storyline again but this time as some kind of otherworldly mercenarie riding Dragons/Giants/Griffins or whatever into battle. I have certainly rushed though this game hard and as such its making me struggle to determine whether its price is justified. The extra story is certainly good, and I've shared my good opinion of the changes that have been made, but truth be told if you own a PS3, you could get a majority of the expierience much cheaper buying the original Hundred Years War version.
In final conclusion I would probably say that while this game is good (if you don't mind actually setting it up properly for your computer), unless your buying it as a completely fresh player, you may wanna wait for a Steam sale or a drop in price of some sorts to fully enjoy the new storyline. Otherwise feel free to buy it as it is, a fun and good game that might be a touch overpriced at £50 but certainly going to keep you busy if have not played the original. I mean lets face it, its unlikely your going to blaze through it quickly and have time to enjoy it properly anyway, right? Its not £50 your investing into a 6 hour game (as most of us gamers have done) its £50 you'll be investing in a good amount of hours worth of play :D

This game was pretty fun.
You start out small, just getting a fresh version of Hacknet's OS from someone named "Bit". Bit is now dead, and it's up to you to find out what caused their death. You go from some simple script kiddie porthacking vulnerable machines and gathering programs to changing IP addresses, popping servers down like it's nothing, deleting system files and bricking machines like it's going out of style. You go from a kid with a legoset to a demon with a supercomputer filled with all sorts of port-cracking programs.
+Learning Curve is perfect.
+Lots to read if you don't mind a bit of work
+Getting extra port-opening programs is extremely fun, especially finding the hard-to-get ones ;)
+You feel like a baller hacker by the end of the game
+Finding programs feels awesome, you earned these port-crackers kiddo
+Forkbombing people after wiping their drive never gets old
+Hacking honeypots without your x-sys is a nice challenge. Only dweebs need a GUI.
+S O U N D T R A C K
+Tracekill.exe
+/-Only one active tracer in the game, unlocks /el though...
+/-Why does notes.exe take up so much RAM??!?!?!
+/-No option to post on /el
-Deleting logs does nearly nothing, and is needed for only one specific part of the game. (Two if you count Academic logs but I never tried that.) It feels like leaving a trail of IPs isn't really that big of a deal because local sysadmins do not care about back-tracing you and deleting you off the map like they should.
-Some missions are convoluted near the end, requiring very specific triggers to get to the next part of the ending mission.
-There is no cause/effect system in the game. This is the worst offender. I feel as if I should be punished for bringing down a major international email server, a major OS development website/server, two security software companies, and /el in under 10 minutes. I at least feel as if picking a fight with /el would be like picking a fight with a group of senior football players in high school as a freshman.
-No achievement for beating the game in terminal-only mode, the ability to play with nothing but a pad and pen listing the J-mail IP address, the terminal, and "help".
-Changing IP is too easy, there needs to be additional layers of security every time you break in.
-No way to access Proxy busters from Terminal view.
-Forkbombing someone without any of their server files should wipe them from the map permanently.

To be fair Uplink is better. This game is good because you get to use the keyboard. Uplink is a hacking game where keyboard is not used, so the biggest flaw is now solved. Problem is the game lacks a bit of adrenaline.
1) Most servers don't trace you, so you can just hang around forever.
2) Its not clear where you are connected too. Once you hack a place is there opened forever. You don't even have to disconnect.
3) You clear your logs but not the disconnected log, which makes no sense. In Uplink you have to clear logs at origin and destination, seems more realistic.
4) Its too easy to go up the ranking.
5) In Uplink you had money to worry about. Upgrade hardware and buy software. In Hacknet all you get is reputation, that also have no impact besides gettings invitations.
6) The game does not allow you to accept more than 1 mission.
7) The storyline is a bit broken. I made 1 mission that lead to a hacker invading my computer, that leads to another mission and to another mission and basically you cannot accept other mission while the "story" is leading you in 1 way. That made me join an organization and now I cannot finish the old missions. Basically I lost 3 missions, cannot be played.
8) The game UI is a bit limited. I cannot open a file and an email at the same time. Which makes very annoying to take note to things. Althought I cannot complain much on that, as in Uplink I really had a pen and paper next to me all the time, in this game I never used real paper so far.
9) Uplink allow you to do other stuff, such as Stock Market, browse any server, etc. Hacknet is limited. You only get the servers IP when the game wants you to get. There is not freedom besides follow the story.
10) Uplink allows you to choose which mission to make, in the sense of choosing to be a good or a bad hacker. In Hacknet some missions presentation don't have more than 2 lines. You have to accept missions without even knowing what skills you need, what tools you need and what you have to do. Its really 1 path only. And if you try to get missions in different orders you lose them, just like I lost 3. UPDATE: Because of this 1 path only + cannot accept more than 1 mission, you can game over all the time. If you delete the wrong file, edit the wrong record, its finished. People call this bug in the forum, I call this lack of flexibility. In Uplink you could simply give up on a mission and pay a fine. If you delete a file you are suppose to upload, it shouldn't be game over, just some kind of punishment.
11) It uses Unix commands but limit them. For instance you have rm command but cannot be used to delete folders. Cannot download folders either.
12) Find it a bit weird that no special software is required to know when you are being traced.
13) So far the challenge of the game seems to be more about curiosity of the player. Meaning you have to look into every folder and file and read and see what you can find (be aware) rather than having a challenge on the hacking it self, such as limited time, required software, go throught LAN networks, etc.
14) You can hack a webserver, a main frame, a home pc or a cell phone, they all look the same, they all have same file structure, they are all hacked with same tools. A bit boring no?
15) Network map completely unecessary. Its just a harder way to find servers, if you are not going to use it to bounce like Uplink, why have that? Just a window with animated blue balls. A list with a search box and some favorites would do the job, or better, connect always using the line command, IP or name assigned by the user.
16) Once you scan a server and it reveals other computers connected to that, more "balls" appears and its a mystery why some are very distant and some are very close. The distance is based on what? It simple confuses the player as it adds a connection between them and with time the connections cross each other. Well, still trying to figure out why did it this way.
17) I'm already playing this game for hours and all I do is execute programs to open ports.
The good:
a) Very well done interface in the sense that keyboard and mouse usage is well integrated. The key here is keyboard. Its very nice to be able to play the entire game using keyboard only.
b) I like the fact that webserver have website with real images. Just because its a hacker game, it doesn't mean the "normal" internet doesn't exist. Although limited, I liked the
.
c) You can see an effort to bring interesting content to see around. Most servers have files that are not crucial to the missions, things you can read, chats, funny stuff. That really adds to the game and was one of the things I feel lacking in Uplink. Perhaps this is one of the reason a lot of servers don't have tracing mechanism, so you don't have time pressure all the time.
d) Not having time pressure all the time is good, but also removed money pressure and other stuff, which is left it a bit unbalanced.
e) Nice animations. The screens change a lot. Its not the same interface all the time.

Absolutely awesome little hacking game. The aesthetic is really solid, hitting that sort of 'near-future/near-past' UI space that most hacking games strive for. If you've ever worked in a *NIX environment, you'll feel right at home. The music is another spot where this game really nails it, has this really gritty cyberpunk feel to it. Also features one of my favorite Carpenter Brut tracks, Roller Mobster.
As for gameplay, it's pretty straightforward. You're sent an email from a dead hacker's failsafe asking you to look into his death. You work your way into various hacker organizations, acquire new tools, and push the story forward. The early missions tend toward the trivial if you've ever worked in a *NIX environment, but once you get into the later missions, putting together the pieces becomes more important than just breaking into servers and rummaging around.
If I had to compare it to anything, I'd say it reminded me quite a bit of Uplink: Hacker Elite and Digital: A Love Story. Uplink is the obvious comparison and HackNet takes a lot of queues from how Uplink's story was told and presented to the player. Digital does a lot of this, too, with the way players have to use the things they find to dig up more clues. I'd say HackNet's story is more similar to Digital in how it sets and escalates stakes, overall. So if you like either or both of those? This is a no-brainer.
Really great experience, doesn't overstay its welcome, but gives you plenty to do and ways to make you feel clever.

I'm going to give this a thumbs up....but just barely. A more honest title for this game would be RNG Path Finder: Alien vs. Marines edition.
Pros:
-Great class system, lots of customization
-The early-mid part of the game feels like you're constantly about to lose, which is pretty much what I was looking for in this game.
-Great graphics and generally engaging gameplay (aside from the optimization con)
-Story / metagame is good enough, and becomes great when considered in context of its impact on how the missions play out
Cons:
-Harder difficulties are only a challenge to the limits of save scumming, not actual strategic skill. And that's not because I'm bad at the game or anything -- the combination of very high damage on both sides, extreme penalties for injuries, and timed missions means that you often MUST get close to perfect rolls. And the seed doesn't change, so you just keep trying♥♥♥♥♥♥and reloading until you hit enough shots to neutralize all the enemies / dodge everything they try to do to you if not. There's no time.
-Bad optimization. I played shortly after release, so this may have been improved.
-Long load times. Between that and the previous 2 issues, I probably spent 50% of my time in the game waiting for something.
So, if you like tactical games this'll probably be worth at least one playthrough. There is a certain satisfaction to finding the thing that will work out perfectly 20% of the time so that you only have to reload a battle 5 times. And it's aliens vs marines

Bonfires are over complicated and not explained very well (yes i know there not really bonfires).
Overall its not worth the asking price, but is definetly worth considering if on sale.

The graphical resembelance to a comic book that this game has its roots from not only creates a unique look and feel; but adds to the ambience and beautiful specialness of this game. You'll be left speechless. Left doubting and regretting decisions you make. You'll be left in utter shock and heartbreak of losing your friends throughout the struggle to survive. You become so immersed within not just the plot, but the game itself that you feel genuine emotion and pain.
It is so fear inspiring, hate inducing and tear wrenching that you will be left struggling to make some very hard decisions that you must face. Don't bother basing your purchase on reading the reviews because no feedback or write up could ever do this game justice. A lot of work went into this game and it shows. I think there should of been a TINY little bit more interactivity within the game; however the second series does so they have clearly been listening to players feedback. I wouldn't consider this a video game. I see it more as a movie where you, the viewer, have a massive impact on the lives and story that plays out.
It takes about 13 - 16 hours to play through the chapters; but the themes, the story, the characters and the emotions will stay with you for ever. My favourite storyline for a video game has been between Metal Gear Solid and Mass Effect, and has been for years. After only the third chapter of this game; it became the best story I've ever seen, game, movie, television included. Dare I say it, it is even better than The Walking Dead TV series itself as you have so much more love for the characters as you become a part of it.
This game will leave you emotionally drained. Do not expect an easy ride as your mistakes will not only carry forward through the game, but to the next series. But most of all a mistake could result in the death of a character you care very much about. And that. That is what you take away from it the most. A genuine sense of loss and grief for the characters you begin to think the world of. It takes a lot to cause genuine upset in this gamer. But it had me on the edge of tears, and I'm not afraid to admit it.
Just promise me that when you get this (because you will), that you will do everything in your power to save these characters. But sometimes...sometimes trying isn't enough...
98/100

First away: I recommend you do NOT spend the full price. I have several dozen hours in Demon Souls and Dark Souls 1, over 200h on Dark Souls 2 and about 100 in Bloodborne on record. The game is simply not worth 50€/$ even if someone likes it. It's to poorly executed in gameplay.
First the Pros:
Graphics an Art Style are pretty neat. The game looks really good but that takes a lot of hardware. Still, looks better than Dark Souls 2 Sotfs or even Bloodborne in my opinion (only graphic wise, not atmospheric). The armors and weapons have a nice design and destinct look each, sharp textures as far as i could tell (playing on 1920x1080).
They have some nice ideas gameplay wise like the reduced stamina cost for the next attack when you time it right or the exp multiplier. I like that and would appreciate it in future Souls games.
And... thats it.
The Cons:
If you expect a precise battle system like the ones from Dark Souls or Bloodborne you will be very disappointed. The attacks of nearly all enemies hit you even if they are already finished an the hit zones are much to large compared to the looks of the attacks. You take damage even if you are way away from an enemy.
You can't "trick" them by learning their patterns and use fast weapon swings in between to stagger them - apparently the don't have poise. They only get staggered by really hard hits like the strong sprint attack, but you can't combo after those attacks an you are completely open for a hit and take guaranteed damage. Enemies aren't really "open" after an attack, each of them has basically only 1 attack after which you can strike them and are designed and scripted to work that way, There are no nuances in that and no variation depending on the weapon you use. It's scripted when you can hit enemies regardless of weapon choice. So just take the biggest and wait.
You can't circle enemies because every attacks aims newly on you and they turn on spot in a fraction of a second without an animation, the basically float while attacking. So dodging, even if you hit the invincibility frame (where ever that is, never found it), will get you no where 'cause you have to dodge all of the 3-4 swings of an enemy combo and will be completely out of stamina when  you are done.
You on the other side will get staggered from every. single. hit. Even the tiniest slap from the fist of an weak archer will completely stop any of your movements even in full sprint trying an onslaught attack on them with an leap attack. You look like a 300 pound tank with a big♥♥♥♥♥axe, sprint towards them, jump an leap your weapon over your head and the they slap you for like 3 damage and stun you out of the air to the ground.
Plus enemies are extremely fast in everything they do compared to you. Even your 1-handed sword swings are slower than a giant long reach swing attack of an enemy with a huge weapon.
So: The balancing in speed and poise is complete off. Enemies are made harder simply because the rule that apply to you don't apply to them.
Damage wise it's the same thing. Once you beat the 4th boss and get back into the Monastery you will meet the first boss again as a trash mob. You will have found the all new griffin armor with really nice defense values. Still, this "new" trash mob here can easily one-shot you. A trash mob. ONE SHOT. I get it that an ex-boss deals a lot of damage and should be dealt with care. But this is not acceptable. Off course you can beat him, you did it earlier so it's not a real problem here, but this is a perfect example of how badly balanced the whole game is. Oh and by the way: The Swing from above (which is the attack that will deal 300 damage flat) has an area off effect that damages you even if you are not close to the hit. And I mean sideways, I'm very aware of the floor ray that extends the attacks length and I'm not talking about that.
I bought the game because a lot of reviews were quite positive, from users and from magazines. But Deck13 is still where they were before this games release: B-Class studio, not even A, and far away from AAA titles.
They probably thought the battle system depends on giving the player disadvantages in every aspect of the game, but forgot to add possibilities to overcome them.
They took the battle system from Souls and ♥♥♥♥ed up balancing, timing, speed and hit zones.
Every one who played a decent amount of the Souls games has a better understanding of this battle system and how the balancing should work out. Deck13 made a very, very poor attempt to copy that and failed massively. Souls veterans will most likely be disappointed  and newcomers will be confronted with very poor execution of the genre and might get repelled to try the good examples.
The camera bobbing from hell annoys as well and can't be turned off. Like on the frigging Titanic.

Alpha Review: Not representative of Final Product
Fractured Space. What a game. I have bought 3 copies of the game, one Vanguard for myself and 2 Forerunner packs for friends. I've been a living, breathing advertisement for Fractured space and so far everyone I have recommended it to have agreed with me. Fractured Space is addicting.
Gameplay - 9/10
I want to give the gameplay 10/10 but I feel like some of the cooldowns are a little long when compared to others. For example the Phantom Ghost (And by extension the Ghost) has such a long cooldown on it's primary missles, which means after Ambush -> Missles you have to wait much longer than everyone else to start firing again. There are of course a few minor issues with balance with some ships but as for an Alpha game the game is amazing.
The gameplay revolves around huge Space Battleships BLOWING EACH OTHER UP. What's not to like?
Graphics - n/a
I will give it n/a because there isn't many textures in the game. There are the asteroids, ships, mining/base ships and an endless expanse of space. Yeah. Exactly. With what we have, the graphics are great so there is no problem but I can't really review it.
Matchmaking - 8/10
I like the matchmaking, not sure why there is an MMR system with no ranks but oh well. The queues can take a while and I can't seem to stop the queue if I want to invite someone or search for Frontline/Conquest instead of vice versa. The games seem balanced usually but there needs to be a penalty for Disconnecting. In too many games does someone disconnect and there is only a 30% faster respawn time. We should get a damage buff for the loss of manpower too. If not then at least add a bot. It's better than nothing.
Progression - 8/10
The progression seems rather slow. I can't seem to discern how your performance changes your exp/credits earned because it seems about the same whether you win or lose (the only difference being you earn massively less when you lose). Then the exp for each faction takes forever to earn. I know you don't want people running around in the best ships right off the bat but it feels like I have been grinding for ages to earn my Watchmann.
Overall score 9/10
I REALLY want to give the game 11/9 but with the few problems that I mentioned above (as well as some FPS issues and PING which doesn't make sense. I get 200ping on London servers and 100ping on further away servers. I don't understand myself) however the game is a definite must buy. If they add a campaign it would only make the game better but I feel like they are going to go the Counter Strike route and not add a story, and just focus on the ships and gameplay which is already pretty polished. I've seen games in beta run less smooth..

METAL SLUG X is an upgraded version of Metal Slug 2. This game made it's way onto PC late last year, but has actually been out since March 1999. This remastered version aimed to increase the difficulty and resolve a couple of the technical faults the original had.
Some of the other improvements such as altered music, more variety on power ups, as well as day/night versions of all of the levels.
The gameplay in METAL SLUG X is almost identical to the other games in the series, it is a run and gun side scrolling platformer. I played METAL SLUG 3 earlier this year, and it felt as if I was just playing that again in terms of gameplay.  At the start of the game you can choose how many lives you have depending on how you want the game to be. Throughout each level, you'll need to help prisoners escape captivity as well as find power ups and weapons for your character.  Each of the weapons have their own feel and have their own advantages and disadvantages so you have to choose wisely.
Difficulty wise, METAL SLUG X is as hard as you want to make it, personally I played through it on Normal difficulty but with unlimited lives - this essentially means you will finish the game since you can just keep dying over and over again without any repercussions apart from a lower score.  The hardcore gamers out there will probably enjoy the fact you can set your self to have either 20, 15, 10 or even 5 credits per run through!
Each stage has its own atmosphere and feel to it, which is something which a lot of side scrolling games like this has. I personally enjoyed the Egypt style level as if you get killed by a Mummy, rather than dying, you actually come back to life as a Mummy yourself, which was a nice little feature to see.
A full playthrough of the single player story took me just under an hour, which to be honest was a little disappointing. I would of at least like to have seen this last at least two or three hours but you can get more mileage out of the game if you ramp up the difficulty I suppose.  We also see CO-OP making a big play in this game as well, you are able to play local or online co-op of the story mode which is something I always like to see in games.
I had no major issues while playing, you can play METAL SLUG X in higher resolutions at 60 fps, not much more you can ask from a game like this.
This game is something I will recommend, but only with the warning on that you have to want to replay the game on higher difficulties or play co-op to get your moneys worth out of it. If you just want to play it for the single player story, you aren't going to get your money/times worth out of the hour long single player, OR, wait for this game to hit the sales, I managed to get mine for mega cheap on the summer sale, so the £1.99 price tag was well worth it for me.
1) Stay away
3) Recommended
4) Highly recommended
5) This is a must play

review about the game.
As I am writing this one down, I have already played for 23 hours, and finished the main missions. I must say that there is not much of a shock to what would I see. The game still has the typical Assassin's Creed feel. If there's anything new that I liked, it would be the
ability. Now you don't have to find a haystack to get down safely.

Now if you don't have a PC with the latest GPUs in the market (and you prefer
over
), I suggest that you

It's just that it requires high-end specs to run it smoothly on the highest settings (thus, the reason for the heavy system requirements). I have a decent gaming laptop (msi ge60 2pe apache pro), but I play on 1280x720 resolution, on medium settings just to get a more stable gameplay. Now, why did I buy (even pre-ordered) the game? Even though I am uncertain of how good/bad the game will be performance wise, I think the reason why I bought this game is because I am a long-time AC fan, and I would not like to miss this game. I do not care if my graphics are not super-duper realistic, as long as I can play this game again after months of waiting.
Well I guess that's about it.

The graphical resembelance to a comic book that this game has its roots from not only creates a unique look and feel; but adds to the ambience and beautiful specialness of this game. You'll be left speechless. Left doubting and regretting decisions you make. You'll be left in utter shock and heartbreak of losing your friends throughout the struggle to survive. You become so immersed within not just the plot, but the game itself that you feel genuine emotion and pain.
It is so fear inspiring, hate inducing and tear wrenching that you will be left struggling to make some very hard decisions that you must face. Don't bother basing your purchase on reading the reviews because no feedback or write up could ever do this game justice. A lot of work went into this game and it shows. I think there should of been a TINY little bit more interactivity within the game; however the second series does so they have clearly been listening to players feedback. I wouldn't consider this a video game. I see it more as a movie where you, the viewer, have a massive impact on the lives and story that plays out.
It takes about 13 - 16 hours to play through the chapters; but the themes, the story, the characters and the emotions will stay with you for ever. My favourite storyline for a video game has been between Metal Gear Solid and Mass Effect, and has been for years. After only the third chapter of this game; it became the best story I've ever seen, game, movie, television included. Dare I say it, it is even better than The Walking Dead TV series itself as you have so much more love for the characters as you become a part of it.
This game will leave you emotionally drained. Do not expect an easy ride as your mistakes will not only carry forward through the game, but to the next series. But most of all a mistake could result in the death of a character you care very much about. And that. That is what you take away from it the most. A genuine sense of loss and grief for the characters you begin to think the world of. It takes a lot to cause genuine upset in this gamer. But it had me on the edge of tears, and I'm not afraid to admit it.
Just promise me that when you get this (because you will), that you will do everything in your power to save these characters. But sometimes...sometimes trying isn't enough...

Dustforce truly is a work of art. I don't mean that lightly. The way it's animated plus its music gives it that title in my book. I can find myself playing one level for an hour, maybe even hours at a time. The frustration of losing levels is filled with relaxation and calmness because of the ambient music. The way the levels are crafted is truly mindblowing. They had a system in which you had to perfect a level to earn a key, and you would use that key to earn more levels. In layman's terms, to earn more levels, you had to perfect current levels. They ditched that and added an XP system in which you gain more XP to earn a key the more levels you play and perfect. I'm very glad they added this system and was skeptical about buying it. But now that I did buy it, I do not regret it even for a second. One thing I really love about this game is how you don't have to unlock base levels. In a sense, this game is open world. That sense is that many levels are available to you, and you can choose whether you want to advance into more challenging levels, or stay where you're at. To get an S in completion, you have to sweep up EVERY leaf, and to get an S in Finesse, you have to maintain your combo throughout an entire level.
Another thing I absolutely enjoy about Dustforce is its expasive community. There are lots of Community Workshop maps for you to sharpen your skills on, and lots of people who can set a good example. I'm sure most of the people who get best times on all the levels have a Youtube channel, so you can probably catch them there. The community may or not be active, but it sure is good and friendly.
Overall, in terms of gameplay, music, artstyle, animation, and difficulty (it's not an easy game, but it's not that hard of a game either. It just depends on how much you want to play it), I rate this game:
10/10
BUY THIS GAME.

Summary - this is still the best bus simulator around.
Pros:
1. Realistic driving.
2. Carefully researched routes.
3. Very realistic buses, with all of their features and with most meticulous attention to detail.
4. Many different buses modelled and quite some routes.
5. You can really see how the world was changing. I especially like to see how different Berlin was before and after the German Unification. The contrast between the West Berlin and the former German Democratic Republic is amazing.
6. Maps are really nicely done.
7. The customization offers you some really HUGE possibilities - with all those different ratios of AI car, pedestrian, parked cars spawning rates and various objects rates you can depict any time of the day, adjust settings to the capabilities of your PC, and generally adjust everything to your liking. This feature is truly unparalleled and its a shame that other simulators lack it.
8. Steering wheel works great and was very easy to configure.
9. Sounds are simply great.
10. There are many mods you can download and many different routes and buses to try.
11. You can customize weather A LOT - so many different settings grant a lot of freedom.
12. AI of the cars is really fine and seems realistic, although sometimes can be quite suicidal if you make a mistake - charging to hit you instead of braking.
Cons
1. Stability - the game likes to freeze, altough nothing game-breaking.
2. Passengers - they look horrible and there are only few models out there. This is perhaps the worst thing in the game.
3. Too little variation in AI cars perhaps.

Some of the recent updates might be discouraging for new players, as it made classes cost money...
But don't worry, you can get a few free, one from the start of course, and one more free a mastery rank 3, and yet another at mastery rank 25.
You can also get another one if you use somebody's friend referal code when below 20 mastery, this will help the person who referred you get a few rewards, and give you a class coin in the process.
And if you play RIFT, or decide to try it, there is an early game mission that can give you a free chloromancer- which is a class beloved by many ever since its arrival.
And after all that, I mean after you finished upgrading the gear for the classes you chose, you can buy more classes from other players who decided to trade a class coin they recieved some way or another, these would cost 60K flux, but by the time you have a few good class that you like maxed out it should be a lot easier.
The game is still relatively F2P, but I suppose you may need to focus on one class more than before due to these recent patches.
Anyways,I guess I can give you a small tip.
Get gear with CD/AS (Critical Damage/Attack Speed) in the second slot, there is a chaos forge which lets you change all but the first and second stats, and those are the most universal and important stats. (AS won't help a Tomb Raiser or Dracolyte though, so try for CD in the second slot) if you don't have CD/AS in the second stat you might end up regretting it later in.
The game also has a sandbox aspect I suppose, you can build in clubworlds, save for if it's been restricted to officers or architects and you are below that rank in the club, and you also have a small cornerstone, which is basically a portable house that  you can place it down anywhere you see a Cornerstone plot. ( Big black square with a sign that has a " ? " on the front. )
Sometimes people go big tall and complicated, othertimes small and fancy, it can be anything you want, get creative or keep it simple, your choice!
Hope you have as much fun as I do when I play it, there's lots to do and the further in you get the more fun you'll have...

I'm going to give this a thumbs up....but just barely. A more honest title for this game would be RNG Path Finder: Alien vs. Marines edition.
Pros:
-Great class system, lots of customization
-The early-mid part of the game feels like you're constantly about to lose, which is pretty much what I was looking for in this game.
-Great graphics and generally engaging gameplay (aside from the optimization con)
-Story / metagame is good enough, and becomes great when considered in context of its impact on how the missions play out
Cons:
-Harder difficulties are only a challenge to the limits of save scumming, not actual strategic skill. And that's not because I'm bad at the game or anything -- the combination of very high damage on both sides, extreme penalties for injuries, and timed missions means that you often MUST get close to perfect rolls. And the seed doesn't change, so you just keep trying♥♥♥♥♥♥and reloading until you hit enough shots to neutralize all the enemies / dodge everything they try to do to you if not. There's no time.
-Bad optimization. I played shortly after release, so this may have been improved.
-Long load times. Between that and the previous 2 issues, I probably spent 50% of my time in the game waiting for something.
So, if you like tactical games this'll probably be worth at least one playthrough. There is a certain satisfaction to finding the thing that will work out perfectly 20% of the time so that you only have to reload a battle 5 times. And it's aliens vs marines

At turns, hopeful and heartbreaking.  It's been a long time since a game or a book hit me this hard.  I don't think I'll ever forget it. You'll spend the next hour wondering if you chose the right thing to do or to say, and you'll probably never know.  I think there's a second season out now; it may be a while before I'm up to tackling the game again.   When something affects you this deeply, you know it's good.  My hat is off to everyone involved - the writers, artists, sound people, programmers; everyone.  If you want a "game" that will leave marks on your heart for a long time to come, I can't recommend this one enough.

It's hard to think of where to begin with this game. The first thing I will say is that it's worth your money for sure.
Before I get into the review, I'll remind you it's in alpha. There are issues; lag spikes, screen freezes, and the occaisional crash. A select few weapons feel a little overpowered, and I guesstimate that the community is about 800 players large (as of the time of this review).
GAMEPLAY
I've heard this game be described as "a cross between LOL and War Thunder", and I sort of agree. You don't control quick little space-fighters like in other space games, but instead you take command of huge capital ships and frigates. You can even hire different crew members for different jobs, giving your ship unique quirks and bonuses. The voice acting is very well done, and adapts to the situation.
There are lanes that you have to go down with the primary objective being to capture the enemy base. Your team must gather resources by capturing mines in each lane, as well as the Gamma station in the centre of the map. The station gives your team a temporary buff, and only opens every few minutes for capture. You travel between lanes by using your ship's jump drive, as each lane is treated as a seperate sector of space.
You cannot travel between bases and lanes freely, as your jump drive needs to cool down. Each jump is a tactical decision, as there's not much you can do to help a team-mate in another sector if he's in trouble.
The second game mode currently in the alpha is "Frontline", where each team fights in one large sector of space over three mines using randomly assigned ships. Again the enemy team's base must be captured, with sudden death disabling respawns.
Each ship has it's own set of weapons and abilities, and act as the equivalent of "heroes" from LOL. There is no small number of ships either- for an alpha this game has enough variety to keep you occupied for about 120 hours or so. Each player has their own role to play, and team-work is essential to win. Your ships have armour on each side which enemies can break through, and you have to turn your ship to avoid multiplied damage where your armour has been destroyed.
ART
The art is absolutely gorgeous. There is immense intricacy in the ship designs and every piece of equipment has a purpose. The three main ship manufactures (United Space Research, Zarek Industrial, and Titan Defence Systems) all have a unique appearance and feel to them. Each faction is very different in both gameplay and visuals.
USR uses more of a traditional tubular ship design, originating from a space exploratory and research company. They focus on giving each ship a very unique and specialised role. Zarek originate from a mining company, and their ships are modular and sharp. Their silhouettes are quite blocky, and they use re-purposed mining equipment as weapons. Titan Defence Systems are the only company in the game with a military background. Their ships use cutting-edge weaponry, and they bear curved armour that looks to be specialy made for each ship.
The environments are awe-inspiring, and the lighting effects of abilities are of top-quality. When a lot of ships are in a single sector you can see a rainbow of bullets, sythe beams, heal drones and ai fighters/bombers. The textures, although currently missing in a small number of areas, are very well made. Even in alpha this game has some brilliant visuals. The sound is equally as impressive, and you can feel that you're a huge lumbering ship as well as each blast of your weapon systems.
CRITISISMS
There are a few improvements and glitches in the game which I have outlined in the official forums as feedback. At the end of the day this is an early access build, and hiccups are to be expected. There are currently a couple of controversies amongst the community such as the lag issues, but I know that the devs are working hard to solve these issues as soon as they can. They have been brilliant in connecting with the community through livestreams, playing with players, and answering q&a sessions.
SUMMARY
Overall I would absolutely reccomend this game. I had no interest in MOBAs before, but Fractured Space has certainly caught my attention. It's a treat for the eyes, fun to play, and a fantastic change from the normal fast-paced nimble fighter games of the past.

This was his labor of love and does it show. They're still releasing content for it and I myself CANNOT wait for Mulitplayer!

Puzzle Quest - Galactrix
It takes a lot for me not to like a game, maybe it has a cheesy plot or the game is loaded with hackers. The list can go on and on. But Galactrix is a game I really tried to like, I mean I loved Puzzle Quest. This game makes you hate it, and you get the feeling the game hates you right back. I don't mind when I lose but this game takes randomly played moves to a whole new level of "dude... wtf...?". It seems they took the core idea of "Puzzle Quest" and put a space like the spin on it. But so much of the magic is left out and it feels... well hollow. You'll spend most of your time hacking gates, mining and fighting your way through a web of systems that feel generic and plane. The AI is like all Puzzle Quest games, unforgiving to the point where you get the feeling it hates you and your babies.
Here are a few examples of this games logic, just so you know I am being fair.
1. Hacking a gate is a time trial, so you need to match the colors as quickly as you can. Sometimes you'll combo, and you'll start a cycle that just won't stop. This eats your time up and yes you'll combo into the color you need, it doses not happen that often. In fact, it is really rare, but none the less you'll lose to the combo cycle and you'll have to start all over again.
2. Combat is like Puzzle Quest, in fact, it's pretty much the same only everything is lasers and shields. One fight I entered, I didn't even get a single move and the AI made a combo that... with just one move. BOOM! I was dead, he combo-ed into a 203 damage play. I know it seems like I am whining but come on. I didn't even get to make a move, not one single move.
3. When you are on the mini map, or overworld map. You'll sometimes get picked up by people who hate you, so you'll have to either fight the ship or run. I know it doses not seem bad to deal with, but you can get trapped into a cycle that just won't stop. Yes, you can fight but their ships are harder and a little op for just patrol duty. So you'll get picked up again, run picked up again.
Pro – I like mining in this game, it's fun and relaxing. Some of the names of the systems are nods to popular space fairing games. Really, I can't think of anything else.
Con – On top of my top 3 list, the music is bland, the AI hates you, and your family, your families families and every girl you ever kissed plus your mom. The story is really boring and dull. Hacking gates is an over used mini game that is just not fun to play. Enemy ships are always more powerful and better skill then you. Lastly... just random crap that like all Puzzle Quest games, happen for no logical reason.
Verdict – I think the developer had a secret hatred for Puzzle Quest and wanted to get revenge on everyone. If you honestly don't mind everything I had a problem with it, then by all means... pick it up. But I think next time they come out with a Puzzle Quest game, I'll wait on it.

I've fallen in love, and she's an English goth-witch with glasses and gun-heels. This is easily the best game I've played all year. The graphics have aged well enough, the story is top-notch, the controls are great, the set-pieces are epic, and the soundtrack is as bad♥♥♥♥♥ as the protagonist. The game makes use of quicktime events, but they're honestly not too bad. I got stuck on one, but I was only pressing half the button combo. Once I realized that, I passed it immediately.
The combat is by far what here for though. Depending on how many techniques you've learned, how good you get at dodging, and what weapons you assign to your hands and heels, you can unleash a nearly endless and unstoppable forray of fury. The number of different ways to string moves together into combos is just insane (and nearly all moves vary depending on weapon load-out) and that's just the top layer. After that there's what're called "Torture Moves" and they work a lot like Mortal Kombat X Brutalities. And you also have the ability to open inter-dimensional gateways to Inferno using her hair, summoning forth nightmare monstrosities. Oh, did I mention that she has to get practically naked in order to do that last bit? No? Well, that's a thing here too. And although that sounds strange, it makes sense once you start playing and get into the story.
Not only do I recommend this game, if you liked the original Devil May Cry series, God of War, or Oni-Musha, then I straight IMPLORE you to pick this one up. It's made by SEGA, but you could've fooled me; it definately feels like a classic Capcom title. As a final note; this is one of only a handful of games ever where the end credits actually deliver everything you wanted, but didn't get throughout the game. I would totally buy Bayonetta 2 if Nintendo ever allowed it to come to PC.

Let me start out by saying that, for me, this is a good game and I've played 60 hours of it in the one week i have it, the game is beyond great but if you came here from the first one, just now that you'll find something different, this game is by far the most linear souls game out there, its like the undead asylum is firelink shrine, and I mean that literally cause the game went as far as to use the same hub name as the first game, not a huge deal but it'll foreshadow the rest of the game, cause every place in this game is a reiteration of some area from a previous game, they sure as hell look different but in most cases they lack the creativity and originality from not only the first game, but also the second. Dont get me wrong, the game has great areas and the level design in this game is by far the best in the souls series, with loads of shortcuts to discover, and every area has that layer of verticality that made the first game so unique. That being said, its time to talk about the worst thing in this game in my opinion, the game has no interconnectivity at all, the game plays like a linear game and that wouldn't be a problem at all if the game wasn't a sequel to a game that set the standard for connected worlds that just fit perfectly together, the lack of verticality and connectivity was already lacking in the second game, but it seems From Software hasn't heard any of the complaints about it, although I have hopes that the next From game will have it cause maybe they haven't heard the map design feedback cause dark souls 3 and bloodborne were being already made at the same time right after the development of dark souls 1 and they were trying to please fans of demon souls that wanted a nexus back, so maybe they hear us out again, idk, I got high hopes for it. But I digress, the point is, the game plays very linearly and at a point, the map just kinda divides in two, meaning that you cant really just walk your way through it all without having to see some loading screens for some areas. It seems like I dislike the game but it's not the case, gameplay wise, the game is arguably the best souls game (not including bloodborne, haven't played it), and it mixes the best things in two with the close to perfect formula from the first one, while adding some new mechanics that mix things up and make it feel real fresh, like the new weapon arts, more phases for bosses and the well needed nerf for magic, making it so that the game isn't a cake walk with a catalyst and a few soul arrows.
This game fixes many things wrong with dark souls 2, but it doesn't bring back many of the things that made the first one so compelling, instead it brings a few problems from the first game too, like the lack of original armor sets when compared to sotfs and infusions now suck♥♥♥♥♥♥again like in dark souls 1. Overall, a great experience but you cant help but wander how much they can learn from this game to make the next one even better.
PS: If you're a souls veteran, this game might not be as hard. For me, it felt like I was already prepared for the challenges that the game was throwing at me due to my hours in dark souls 1 and sotfs, it didnt convey the same sense of fear from the world that I had in the first game

Cons:

Some of the recent updates might be discouraging for new players, as it made classes cost money...
But don't worry, you can get a few free, one from the start of course, and one more free a mastery rank 3, and yet another at mastery rank 25.
You can also get another one if you use somebody's friend referal code when below 20 mastery, this will help the person who referred you get a few rewards, and give you a class coin in the process.
And if you play RIFT, or decide to try it, there is an early game mission that can give you a free chloromancer- which is a class beloved by many ever since its arrival.
And after all that, I mean after you finished upgrading the gear for the classes you chose, you can buy more classes from other players who decided to trade a class coin they recieved some way or another, these would cost 60K flux, but by the time you have a few good class that you like maxed out it should be a lot easier.
The game is still relatively F2P, but I suppose you may need to focus on one class more than before due to these recent patches.
Anyways,I guess I can give you a small tip.
Get gear with CD/AS (Critical Damage/Attack Speed) in the second slot, there is a chaos forge which lets you change all but the first and second stats, and those are the most universal and important stats. (AS won't help a Tomb Raiser or Dracolyte though, so try for CD in the second slot) if you don't have CD/AS in the second stat you might end up regretting it later in.
The game also has a sandbox aspect I suppose, you can build in clubworlds, save for if it's been restricted to officers or architects and you are below that rank in the club, and you also have a small cornerstone, which is basically a portable house that  you can place it down anywhere you see a Cornerstone plot. ( Big black square with a sign that has a " ? " on the front. )
Sometimes people go big tall and complicated, othertimes small and fancy, it can be anything you want, get creative or keep it simple, your choice!
Hope you have as much fun as I do when I play it, there's lots to do and the further in you get the more fun you'll have...
At least, that's been my experience.

XCOM 2
Release Date: February 5, 2016
Strengths:
-Originality
-Very good graphics
-Good level design and gameplay
-Super cool enemies
-Great replayability because of random generation of maps and enemies each time
-Great story and characters
-Excellent sound and voice acting
-More detailed character and team customizations
-Resource management and economy based
-Research technologies and build new weapons, armours etc
Limitations:
-Turn based so takes a lot of play time so RTS lovers may not like it
-Limited DLC
Conclusion:
XCOM 2 is a sequel to the legendary XCOM: Enemy Unknown which is one of the best turn based strategy games out there.  The gameplay is similar to the previous XCOM with some changes like- better graphics, more custumizations for characters, new characters and abilities, new type of missions, new weapons, new enemies etc.  Its more of a newly skinned XCOM with a refreshing new interface and campaign.  In terms of atmosphere and eerieness, I liked "Enemy Unkwown" better. This being said, XCOM 2 is not a bad game either. It is sufficiently changed to give the players a new challange without tempering with the core mechanics of the game which made it stand out in the first place. The graphics are probably the best part of the game and at maximum setting makes the game look extremely good. Enemies are very well designed and the game is very challanging in hard mode. So if you like challange, strategic gameplay and resource management, this is one of the best games available today. Definitely recommended.

Pros:
-Great class system, lots of customization

So..Starbound.  Where to start?
Well, I've decided to come back and change the review on a game that I've not only played more than any other, but also because a recent massive update has changed the game to make it far more refined.
tl;dr  If you like terraria, space games, or sandbox games, then this is for you.  You won't be disappointed.  This game has a ton of content already to keep you entertained for hours, and constant updates from the devs will always leave you with something to do.
Firstly, yes this game is and has been an early access game for a LONG time.  I know.  However, the devs have not only updated a constantly changing list of all they want implemented/changed before they feel comfortable releasing the game as finished.  They also constantly update their website with artwork, coding, and new content in general. They are still very active and even recently gained a new dev or two to further increase production on the game.
Now, like mentioned in the tl;dr, this game is a lot like Terraria.  I'm pretty sure that one of the artists that worked on Terraria is working on this one as well, so that's why they look similar.  This certainly doesn't mean they are the same game, however.  While both are sandbox's, Starbound has a map system that allows you to explore new planet systems based on technology you have available.  For example, once you gain the tech to breathe without any oxygen, you can visit moons.  This is, in my opinion, already far superior to the one world you are allowed in Terraria.
Now, you can build a lot of cool structures in this game, or take over dungeons on the surface and convert them into your own.  As of right now, unfortunately, the dev's have only really completed the nomad route of the game, so there isn't much of a reason to build on a planet.  They have stated that they intend to add more possible play styles in the future, however.
One such playstyle is that of a farmer, which they are currently working on.  A recent update has added MASIVE amounts of food and crafting recipes so you can cook up pretty much any food (within reason, of course) that you can imagine.  Various food gives you buffs, and the more ingredients used, the better the buffs will be.
Your ship, which is used to navigate to different plants/systems, can be upgraded later in the game to be far bigger, with multiple rooms, thus supporting the style of nomad.  This is important because you will get a ton of furniture and other items that you totally think you'll use one day in the building of a mega base.  I only ever end up using a little bit of it, but I think that this would happen in any game with literally hundreds of dungeons ripe for the taking.
Enemies vary from planet to planet. Generally all of the flying ones are evil, but not much of a problem unless you find yourself far up in the sky.  One creature will always be passive, and then two or three others will be aggressive.  It changes randomly for every single planet, so you have to discover which is pasive and which are aggressive through your own discovery.
The crafting system will depend somewhat on the race you pick; Apex (ape), Avian (bird), Floran (plant), Glitch (robot), Human (self-explanatory), Hylotl (fish-like), and finally the newest, Novakid (pure energy).  Each has their own style and theme (ex. Novakids are cowboys, Florans are primitive hunters, and Glitch are medievel themed).  Their respective dungeons show this (although there are not currently any Novakid dungeons, that race was only recently introduced).  Your weapons and armor that are crafted will reflect these themes, which I think was a very nice touch.
This review is starting to get really lengthy, so I think I'll wrap it up with the new quest system.  After going through the intro quest to fix your ship (to a degree), you travel to the newly introduced Gate, which will teleport you to a decently sized trading outpost.  The multitude of creatures in there will have various quests that lead you to progress through the game as you go.  Some of them are standard and a little boring, others are creative and funny.
With one or two things left out, I think that sums up Starbound as best as I can sum it up.  Please, support the dev's and buy this game!  The soundtrack, which is beautiful, also comes FOR FREE with the game, and you'll get a free copy of a non-steam version (if you want that) once the game is fully released.  I understand people are upset about it not having been finished when it should have been, but the constant awesome updates make it worth the while. And yes, I have been following this game since it was first "released to the world," so I've seen it all.  Aloha!
